brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit with two drawers (notch drawer frames)
requirements.evidence: Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at (-1,0) and hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at (1,-1)) sit in empty positions beside touching bases (0,0), (0,-1), (1,0). The configurator's 'drawer' family was never offered (it needs a half-base cut face), so these are the notch-type drawers instead.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit built from Hex Cluster parts with shelving storage (bins) for books
requirements.evidence: Bases piece:0,0,0 full, piece:0,-1,0 full, piece:1,0,0 half-e; two 3-compartment full-depth bins (bin:0,0,0 and bin:0,-1,0) as shelving; check_build ok, meshClash clear, 5 parts plus 2 drawer frames and 2 bins within the 40-part limit.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books (load rating; not verifiable by the configurator)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it cannot check load, material strength or print settings. Nothing in the build proves the 50 kg rating; it depends on material, infill and fixings chosen for printing.

finish.summary: Built a small Hex Cluster shelf unit: three bases (full at 0,0 and 0,-1, half-east at 1,0) with two 3-compartment bins as shelving, and two notch drawer frames filling the empty spots beside the touching bases. check_build is ok with a clear mesh check. The 50 kg book rating cannot be verified here and depends on material and printing, so it is unverified.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
